pages.title: Introduction
pages.snippet: UNITEC | TURNING INTRODUCTION TURNING Introduction
pages.text:
UNITEC | TURNING                                                                                                  INTRODUCTION




TURNING

Introduction
Unitec turning inserts and holders cover external turning, facing, profiling and boring of steel,
stainless steel, cast iron, aluminium, heat-resistant alloys and hardened steel - from small
Swiss-type parts to heavy roughing.

 NEGATIVE INSERT              POSITIVE INSERT              EXTERNAL TURNING                             BORING




  Longitudinal turning                                                       Negative inserts
  Most common operation - 80° and 55° inserts with                           Double-sided, 0° clearance, more cutttng edges and a
  93°/95° holders.                                                           stronger edge - first choice for external turning on
                                                                             stable machines.
  Facing
  Machining the end face - 80° inserts, 90°-95° holders                      Positive inserts
  or 45°/75° holders for roughing.                                           Single-sided with 5°-11° clearance - lower cutttng force
                                                                             for small parts, slender workpieces and boring.
  Profiling / copying
  Contours and undercuts - 55° and 35° inserts with
  93°-117.5° holders.
  Boring
  Internal turning - positive inserts on boring bars from
  Ø4 mm minimum bore.


ISO workpiece material groups
  P    Steel                       Low-carbon, medium/high-carbon, alloy and tool steels; ferritic / martensitic / PH stainless steels

  M    Stainless Steel             Austenitic, high-strength austenitic, cast and duplex stainless steels

  K    Cast Iron                   Gray cast iron, ductile / nodular and compacted graphite irons, ADI

  S    High-Temp Alloys            Iron-, cobalt- and nickel-based heat-resistant alloys; titanium and titanium alloys

  H    Hardened Steels             Hardened alloy and tool steels, 44 HRC and above


How to use this catalogue
 1    Identify the material                                                 2     Choose the insert shape
      ISO group P, M, K, N, S or H.                                               Strongest shape the operation allows (80° > 55° > 35°).

 3    Choose the chipbreaker                                                4     Select the grade
      F finishing, M medium, R roughing - see the chipbreaker                      Grade table; order as insert code-chipbreaker + grade.
      guide.

 5    Choose the holder                                                     6     Set vc, f and ap
      External holder or boring bar for the insert and lead                       Cutttng-data page and calculator.
      angle.

UNITEC TURNING GRADES

Grades
Choose the grade series for the workpiece material: UP for steel, UM for stainless steel, UK for
cast iron, UH for heat-resistant alloys and hardened steel, UC cermet for finishing and UN07 for
aluminium.

 Grade              Type      P    M     K    N    S      H   Application

 UP1225              CVD      ●                               General use for steel - wide application range, continuous to interrupted cutttng.

 UP1425              CVD      ●                               Steel, continuous to light interrupted machining at medium to high speed.

 UP1825              CVD      ●                               Steel at high speed with long tool life; finishing and semi-finishing.

 UP1325              CVD      ●                               Steel, heavy interrupted cutttng and high feed rates.

 UC70               Cermet    ●                               General use and quality surface finish; balanced wear and fracture resistance.

 UC90            Cermet+      ●                               Finishing with higher strength; excellent surface finish.

 UM5625              PVD           ●                          Stainless steel - stable at low speed, continuous to heavily interrupted machining.
 UM5825              PVD           ●                          Stainless steel - TiAlN coating with excellent fracture toughness and stability.

 UM5830              PVD           ●                          Stainless steel - low cutttng resistance, reduced adhesion and edge build-up.

 UM1610              PVD           ●                          Stainless steel - sharp positive inserts for small parts.

 UK3030              CVD                ●                     Grey cast iron - first choice; continuous to light interrupted cutttng.

 UK3010              CVD                ●                     Grey cast iron - hard, wear-resistant grade for high speed continuous cutttng.

 UK3020              CVD                ●                     Nodular / ductile cast iron - first choice; tough coating against built-up edge.

 UH724               PVD                           ● ● Inconel, HRSA and hardened steel; also stainless steel.
 UH744               PVD                           ● ● New launch - titanium, Inconel / HRSA and heat-resistant stainless; semi-finish to
                                                       roughing.
 UN07            Uncoated                     ●               Aluminium and non-ferrous metals - sharp, polished edge.
● = grade rated for the ISO material group.

UNITEC | TURNING                                                                                                            CHIPBREAKERS




UNITEC CHIPBREAKERS

Chipbreaker Guide
Each chipbreaker is shown with its application range (depth of cut ap against feed f) and cross-
section. F = finishing, M = medium machining, R = roughing.

   F05 Finishing                                                 NEGATIVE     M10 Medium                                                     NEGATIVE

 Finishing of general steel and alloy steel. Curved, sharp cutttng edge for   Finishing of stainless steel and mild steel. Sharp edge reduces cutttng
 good chip control and a fine surface finish.                                  force for a high-quality surface; low feed, small depth of cut.




   M25 Medium                                                    NEGATIVE     M20 Medium                                                     NEGATIVE

 Stainless steel and heat-resistant super alloys. Sharp edge gives low       Semi-finishing of stainless steel and high-temperature alloys. Variable
 cutttng forces - ideal for thin walls and long shafts.                       rake angle and edge width for sharpness with strength; heart-shaped
                                                                             chip breaker.




   M35 Medium                                                    NEGATIVE     M05 Medium                                                     NEGATIVE

 Semi-finishing of general steel and alloy steel. Strong flat cutttng edge      Semi-finishing of general steel and alloy steel. Gradient, waved hump for
 with good strength.                                                         a wide application range.




   M45 Medium                                                    NEGATIVE     M30 Medium                                                     NEGATIVE

 Semi-finishing of general steel and alloy steel. Large rake angle lowers     Medium cutttng of stainless steel and mild steel. Sharp cutttng edge.
 cutttng force; variable groove depth for excellent chip removal.




   R15 Roughing                                                  NEGATIVE     R25 Roughing                                                   NEGATIVE

 Heavy cutttng of cast iron. Strong cutttng edge and large chip pocket -       Heavy cutttng of carbon steel, cast steel and alloy steel. Variable land
 good at large depth and width of cut.                                       and progressive chip space for lower cutttng force; reinforced straight
                                                                             edge.

UNITEC | PCD INSERTS                                                                                             INTRODUCTION




PCD INSERTS

Introduction
PCD (polycrystalline diamond) is the hardest cutttng material after natural diamond. A PCD tip
brazed onto a carbide insert gives a sharp, wear-resistant edge for non-ferrous and non-
metallic materials, with tool life many times longer than carbide.

 PCD INSERT                           PCD INSERT                            PCD INSERT                        PCD INSERT




Where to use PCD
 Material                                                  Examples                                                 Suitable
                                  Wrought and cast aluminium, Al-Si alloys (pistons, wheels,
 Aluminium alloys                                                                                                    ● Best
                                                        housings)
 Copper alloys                                       Copper, brass, bronze                                              ●
 Composites                                            CFRP, GFRP, MMC                                                  ●
 Non-metals                                  Graphite, plastics, wood composites                                        ●
 Green / sintered
                                                       Pre-sintered parts                                               ●
 carbide
                                                                                                       - Not suitable (diamond reacts with
 Ferrous metals                            Steel, cast iron, stainless, titanium alloys
                                                                                                                       iron)


Benefits
 1     Long tool life                                                         2    Fine finish
       Very high abrasion resistance - ideal for high-silicon                      Sharp, ground PCD edge gives a mirror-like surface.
       aluminium.

 3     High speed                                                             4    Consistent size
       Run at high cutttng speeds on aluminium and copper                           Slow wear keeps parts on size for long runs.
       alloys.


     Note. PCD is for non-ferrous and non-metallic materials only. For hardened steel and cast iron use CBN or
     ceramic.

CERAMIC INSERTS

Ceramic inserts keep their hardness at temperatures where carbide softens. They turn and mill
cast iron, hardened steel and heat-resistant alloys at speeds several times higher than carbide,
with long tool life and a fine finish.

UNITEC | CERAMIC INSERTS                                                                                                    TECHNICAL




CERAMIC INSERTS

Application Tips & Troubleshooting
Ceramic rewards a rigid, well-set-up machine. These rules prevent most edge failures.
   Use the strongest insert shape the job allows: round > 100 deg (W/80       Coolant: apply either dry or full continuous flood - never intermittent.
   deg C) > square > triangle > 55 deg D > 35 deg V (weakest).                White oxide and most hard-turning work is dry; superalloys with
   Choose the largest practical nose radius, thickest insert and a small      SiAlON/whisker use flood.
   entering angle (15-45 deg lead) to spread load and reduce notching.        Do not reduce cutttng speed without also reducing feed - a cold chip
   Ceramics need maximum rigidity: minimum overhang, largest shank,           causes edge chipping; ceramics need heat in the cut.
   heavy-metal or carbide boring bars, good machine condition and             On scale, cast skin or very hard surfaces reduce speed and feed by
   sufficient spindle power.                                                    about 25% until the skin is removed.
   Use holders/clamps designed for ceramics (top clamp or lever with          Vary depth of cut between passes (or ramp) to avoid notch wear at
   carbide seat); tighten with a torque wrench (approx. 4 Nm for small        the same point on the edge.
   clamp screws) - do not over-tighten.                                       Do not run ceramics on titanium (fire hazard and rapid wear) or on
   Seat must be clean and flat; replace damaged shims - point contact          aluminium/non-ferrous; use carbide/PCD.
   cracks ceramic inserts.                                                    Cast iron with ceramics typically runs ~6x the speed of coated
   Never use an up-sharp edge on ceramics; select chamfered (T) or            carbide; superalloys 5-10x - keep speed in range to gain the benefit.
   chamfered + honed (S) edges, heavier for interruptions.                    Leave at least 0.3 mm stock for the finishing pass on superalloys.
   Pre-chamfer the workpiece at entry and exit and reduce feed ~25%

 Spindle speed                         n (RPM)                        n = vc x 1000 / (π x Dc)
 Feed rate                             vf (mm/min)                    vf = f x n
 Parting time                          tc (min)                       tc = (Dc / 2) / vf

pages.text:
UNITEC | MILLING                                                                             HIGH FEED | INTRODUCTION




HIGH FEED MILLING

Introduction
High feed milling uses a small lead angle and shallow depth of cut to direct cutttng forces axially
into the spindle. The result is a thin chip that permits very high feed per insert, exceptional
stability on long overhangs and the fastest metal-removal rates in roughing, pocketing and face
milling.
                                                                          Higher productivity
                                                                          Feed per insert up to 2.0 mm - several times that of
                                                                          conventional face milling.
                                                                          Stable on long reach
                                                                          Axial force direction suits extended holders and weak
                                               axial force, very high v   set-ups without chatter.
                                                                          Longer tool life
                                                                          Thin chips reduce edge loading and heat; wear is spread
                                                                          along the cutttng edge.
                                                                          One tool, many operations
                                                                          Face milling, pocketing, ramping, helical milling and
                                                                          plunging.



                                                                                                                                       HIGH FEED

High feed inserts have a special cutttng-edge profile. For CAM programming, model the cutter

UNITEC | MILLING                                                                                           SPEED & FEED CALCULATOR




FROM CATALOGUE VALUES TO MACHINE PARAMETERS

Speed & Feed Calculator
Take vc and fz from the cutttng-data tables, then convert them into spindle speed, table feed
and metal-removal rate for your cutter with the standard milling formulas below.

Formulas
 Spindle speed                        n (RPM)                        n = vc x 1000 / (π x D)
 Table feed                           vf (mm/min)                    vf = n x fz x z
 Feed per revolution                  f (mm/rev)                     f = fz x z
 Metal removal rate                   Q (cm3/min)                    Q = ap x ae x vf / 1000
vc = cutttng speed (m/min), D = cutter diameter (mm), fz = feed per insert (mm), z = number of inserts, ap = axial depth of cut (mm), ae = radial width of
cut (mm).


Worked example
 INPUTS - P2 steel, APMT 1604 shell mill Ø50, 5 inserts                      RESULTS

 Cutttng speed vc                                  200          m/min          Spindle speed n                           1,273          RPM

 Cutter diameter D                                 50          mm
                                                                              Table feed vf                               955          mm/min

                                                                              Feed per revolution                        0.75          mm/rev
 Number of inserts z                                5          pcs

 Depth of cut ap / width ae                     5 / 35         mm             Metal removal rate Q                        167          cm3/min


n = 200 x 1000 / (3.1416 x 50) = 1,273 RPM; vf = 1,273 x 0.15 x 5 = 955 mm/min; Q = 5 x 35 x 955 / 1000 = 167
cm3/min.

       better surface; use conventional milling only on hard              use the full flute length for even wear.
       scale.

       pressure coolant for stainless, titanium and aluminium.            strong floors; ball nose for 3D surfaces and finishing.

SINGLE-EDGE DRILL - FOR CNC LATHES

SF Single-Edge Drill Bit for CNC Lathes
Special for CNC lathes: one indexable single-edge drill that drills, bores, faces and turns the outer
diameter - fewer tools, fewer tool changes, shorter cycle times.

Benefits                                                                    APPLICATION      Traditional way: three tools

  Turning, boring and drilling - all done with one tool.
                                                                                                              Drilling
  Saves installation time and shortens the tool-change cycle.
  Reduces the number of tools required and saves tool costs.

  On a CNC lathe the traditional way needs a twist drill, an
                                                                                               End-face & OD turning
  end-face / OD turning tool and a boring bar. The SF single-
  edge drill replaces all three: its insert drills from solid, then

pages.text:
UNITEC | DRILLING                                                                              VMD LARGE DRILL | PRECAUTIONS




VMD LARGE DRILL - APPLICATION NOTES

Precautions When Using
   1. Existing holes larger than the pilot drill
On a machined surface like the ones shown below, drilling directly into an existing hole that is larger than the pilot (guide) drill diameter
causes severe vibration and may damage the pilot drill and the inserts.




   2. Inclined surfaces
When the workpiece has an inclined face, first mill the surface flat, then drill.




                                                                                                                                                 VMD LARGE DRILLS
   3. Overlapping workpieces

pages.text:
UNITEC | DRILLING                                                                                         SPADE DRILL | OVERVIEW




SPADE DRILL

Characteristics & Advantages of Spade Drilling
   Introduction
      Unitec's spade drill is an indexable drill with replaceable inserts; inserts can be changed flexibly to suit the diameter, drilling
      depth and workpiece material.
      Spade drills can be used on both conventional machines and CNC machine tools. The drill tip is replaced on the machine, making
      work fast, convenient and far more efficient.
      A spade drill consists of a holder and an insert fixed with screws. The high-precision interface between holder and insert ensures
      accurate insert clamping and easy insert replacement. The holder is made of high-quality steel with good toughness and high
      wear resistance, vacuum heat-treated and tempered. Inserts are made of imported high-end powder high-speed steel (HSS) and
      solid carbide; the cutttng edge has chip-breaking grooves and the tip has a self-centering edge. The holder has an internal coolant
      design and can be connected to the machine's through-coolant system.
      Spade drills offer high efficiency, simple operation and excellent cost-effectiveness: overall drilling efficiency is 2-5 times that of a
      standard twist drill and tool life is 3-5 times longer. Hole tolerance is within +0.05 / -0.05 mm, and drilling depth can reach 25 × D.



   Advantages
      Simple, convenient insert interface - inserts are changed on the machine, saving regrinding time.
      Inserts are available with a range of coatings, covering drilling of stainless steel, structural steel and many other metallic and non-
      metallic materials.
      Holders feature internal coolant, so chips are evacuated promptly and cooling stays effective even when drilling deep holes.
      Only 16 holders cover drilling diameters from ø9.5 mm to ø114 mm. Two shank series - straight shank with side clamping
      (Weldon) and taper shank - give high versatility and easy connection to all kinds of machine tools.



Spade drill selection
The spade drill consists of a holder and an
insert; the centre of the holder has internal
coolant. One holder size accepts inserts of
several sizes, reducing the cost of purchasing
holders.

Inserts come in two series - imported
powder HSS and imported solid carbide.
Please choose the type that suits your
machining conditions.

Assembling the KS Combined Drill
Three steps: fit the centre-edge insert, fit the outer-edge insert and guide strip, then mount the cutter head on the

    2     Fit the outer-edge insert and guide strip onto the cutter head

    3     Mount the cutter head onto the side-fixed tool body

                              both connection systems are of the same specification. Mount the
                              cutter head onto the side-fixed tool body and check that it seats
                              correctly.




                                                             b   Insert the connection-system locking screws on both sides and tighten

UNITEC | BTA DEEP HOLE DRILLING                                                                                       INTRODUCTION




DEEP HOLE DRILLING

Introduction
Unitec BTA tools drill, counterbore and trepan deep holes from ø14 mm to ø328 mm. Coolant is
fed at high pressure to the cutttng edge and the chips are flushed out through the drill tube, so
holes many times deeper than their diameter come out straight, round and with a fine finish.
 BRAZED HEADS                            BTA INSERT                   DEEP-LINE                                  DRILL TUBE

pages.text:
UNITEC | BTA DEEP HOLE DRILLING                                                            BTA SYSTEM | Deep hole drilling head series




INDEXABLE BTA SYSTEM

Deep hole drilling head series
Single Tube System (STS) and Double Tube System (DTS)




   Single Tube System (STS)
   The STS is also referred to as the BTA system in the deep hole drilling process. A large volume of coolant is pumped under high pressure to the cutttng
   area in the workpiece. Chips are then forced out through the drill tube at the back and do not touch the workpiece providing an outstanding surface
   finish. STS is a stable method to create holes with high accuracy by using a dedicated drilling machine and a sealing with the workpiece.
   Double Tube System (DTS)
   The DTS is characterized by its two tube construction and is therefore known as the double tube system. A sealing system and pressure head, which is


                                                                                                                                                            BTA SYSTEM
   required in the Single Tube System (STS), is not necessary for the DTS and it is therefore suitable for conventional general purpose machines such as
   CNC lathes or machining centers.

pages.title: Introduction
pages.snippet: UNITEC | THREADING INTRODUCTION THREADING Introduction
pages.text:
UNITEC | THREADING                                                                                                INTRODUCTION




THREADING

Introduction
Unitec threading tools cover thread turning with laydown inserts and thread milling with
indexable inserts, solid carbide thread mills and deep-hole milling heads - for metric, UN,
Whitworth, pipe, round, trapezoidal and ACME threads.

 THREAD TURNING               THREADING BAR                                MILLING INSERT               SOLID THREAD MILL




  Thread turning                                                           Solid carbide thread mills
  The insert moves along the axis once per revolution, in                  Small threads from M3, very accurate; versions with
  several radial passes. Lowest tool cost; best for lathes                 coolant through, chamfer, and drill + thread + chamfer
  and long threads.                                                        in one tool.
  Thread milling                                                           Deep hole thread milling
  The tool follows a helical path (circular interpolation).                Modular heads on long holders for threads far inside
  One tool makes many diameters, right- or left-hand                       bores and housings.
  threads, and leaves small, controlled chips.

ISO workpiece material groups
  P    Steel                       Low-carbon, medium/high-carbon, alloy and tool steels; ferritic / martensitic / PH stainless steels

  M    Stainless Steel             Austenitic, high-strength austenitic, cast and duplex stainless steels

  K    Cast Iron                   Gray cast iron, ductile / nodular and compacted graphite irons, ADI

  S    High-Temp Alloys            Iron-, cobalt- and nickel-based heat-resistant alloys; titanium and titanium alloys

  H    Hardened Steels             Hardened alloy and tool steels, 44 HRC and above


How to use this catalogue
 1    Thread standard                                                       2     Method
      Metric, UN, Whitworth, BSPT, NPT, NPTF, Rd, Tr, ACME,                       Turning on a lathe, or milling on a machining centre.
      Pg.

 3    Profile                                                                4     Insert / tool size
      Full profile (crests formed) or partial profile (one insert,                  From the pitch and the thread diameter.
      many pitches).

 5    Holder                                                                6     Cutttng data
      External, internal, shank or shell mill for the insert size.                Infeed tables and thread-milling formulas.

pages.text:
UNITEC | THREADING                                                                                                          GRADES




UNITEC THREADING GRADES

Grades
PVD and CVD grades for thread turning and thread milling.

 Grade             Coating and application
                   The PVD-coated central grade is your first choice for ISO P, K, S and H materials and provides excellent wear resistance
 UT923             and toughness.
                   High-performance Ultra-CVD coated grade • Provide stable tool life by preventing any unexpected tool breakage due to
 UH721             application of the new Ultra-CVD coating • Increased chip evacuation due to high-hardness and highly lubricative
                   coating
                   It is a tough submicron PVD TiAlN coated grade. It is suitable for threading at low-to-medium cutttng speeds. This grade
 UT925             has been designed for machining of heat-resistant alloys, austenitic stainless steel, hard alloys and carbon steels. It also
                   performs well with interrupted cuts and under unfavorable machining conditions


   Grade choice. The grade columns on the insert pages show where each grade is stocked (●). Use the tougher
   PVD grade for interrupted cuts, stainless steel and heat-resistant alloys, the CVD grade for continuous turning of
   steel and cast iron, and the uncoated grade for aluminium and non-ferrous metals.

pages.text:
UNITEC | THREADING                                                                                  CUTTING DATA | Thread milling




THREAD MILLING

Thread Milling - Programming & Formulas
Thread milling uses helical interpolation. The feed programmed at the tool centre must be
corrected so the cutttng edge runs at the intended feed per tooth.

 Spindle speed                                  n (RPM)                  n = vc x 1000 / (π x d)
 Feed at the cutttng edge                        vf (mm/min)              vf = fz x z x n
 Programmed feed - internal thread              vf prog                  vf prog = vf x (D - d) / D
 Programmed feed - external thread              vf prog                  vf prog = vf x (D + d) / D
 Axial move per 360°                            (mm)                     = thread pitch P
vc cutttng speed (m/min), d tool cutttng diameter (mm), D thread major diameter (mm), z number of flutes / teeth, fz feed per tooth (mm).


Good practice
 1     Approach                                                                  2   Climb milling
       Enter on a 90° or 180° arc (tangential) to avoid a mark on                    Right-hand internal thread: start at the bottom and climb
       the thread and a sudden load on the edge.                                     upward (G03); right-hand external thread: G02 from the
                                                                                     top down.

 3     Passes                                                                    4   Pitch, not diameter
       Large pitches or hard materials: split the depth in 2-3                       One partial-profile or full-profile tool covers every
       radial passes, or use a spring pass for accuracy.                             diameter of the same pitch - just change the program.



                                                                                                                                                    CUTTING DATA
     Example - internal M16x1.5 in steel, solid carbide thread mill d = 10 mm, z = 3, vc = 120, fz = 0.06: n = 3,820
     RPM, vf = 688 mm/min, programmed feed = 258 mm/min.
General starting values - adjust vc and fz to material, tool size and machine.

UNITEC | TOOL HOLDERS & ADAPTERS                                                                  TECHNOLOGY | DYNAMIC BALANCING




TECHNOLOGY & SELECTION

DYNAMIC BALANCING
THE COST OF POOR TIR AND UNBALANCED HOLDER ON CUTTING TOOLING LIFE IS 20%




   The Cost Of Poor TIR and Unbalanced Holder On Cutttng Tooling Life is 20%
   Dynamic balancing on highly precision German make “” machine at G6.3/G2.5 grade @15000/25000 rpm.
   Ideally, surface finish is determined by feed rates, depth of cut and spindle speed. However, surface finish also is influenced By background vibration
   caused by unbalance mass in tool holder
   Unbalance forces of tool holder can act like additional runout in the subsequent cutttng tool




                                                                                                                                                           TECHNOLOGY
   Tool balance is a key factor to consider for optimizing your cutttng tools' performance. Improperly balanced tools will Cause poor part finish, uneven
   tool wear, reduced tool life, noise and possible machine spindle failure and damage.
   The balance of a rotating tool clamping product is critical to machine spindle wear and cutttng tool performance,
